title: Why Java Doesn't Support Multiple Class Inheritance
summary: Understand the Diamond Problem, deadly ambiguity, and how Composition solves multiple capabilities cleanly.
learningObjectives: Understand why Java forbids 'class C extends A, B'
Explain the Diamond Problem and method ambiguity in simple terms
Analyze state duplication conflicts caused by multiple parent classes
Compare Java's design philosophy with C++ multiple inheritance
Use Composition (HAS-A) as a clean, unambiguous design alternative
expectedOutcomes: Ability to explain the Diamond Problem with crystal clarity in engineering interviews
Understanding of why Java chose simplicity and safety over multiple class inheritance

activities.title: The Conflicting Bosses Analogy
activities.content:
Imagine you work at a company and have two direct bosses: Boss A and Boss B.

At 9:00 AM, both bosses send you an email with the subject: `handleCustomerEmergency()`.
- Boss A writes: *"Issue an immediate 100% refund!"*
- Boss B writes: *"Do NOT refund! Send a replacement item instead!"*

You are standing in front of the customer. Whose instruction do you execute?

You are frozen in complete ambiguity! There is no correct answer unless someone introduces complex, arbitrary rules.

In programming, this exact dilemma is why Java **does not support multiple class inheritance**. If a class could extend two parent classes that define the same method, the computer wouldn't know which method to run!

activities.title: The Diamond Problem and Java's Single Inheritance Rule
Demonstrating the Ambiguity Problem
activities.description: Understand the exact conflict that would occur if multiple class inheritance were allowed.

steps.description: Printer and ScreenDisplay both provide a method with the identical signature: void output().
If a child class extended both, calling c.output() would create complete ambiguity.
The compiler would have to guess or use complicated priority rules.
Java eliminates this confusion at the language grammar level by refusing multiple extends.

activities.codeSnippet: // class Child extends ParentA, ParentB { } // FORBIDDEN!

activities.title: The Clean Solution: Composition Over Inheritance
activities.description: See how Composition (HAS-A) cleanly provides multiple capabilities without any ambiguity.

steps.description: AudioPlayer and VideoRecorder are two independent classes.
SmartCamera does NOT extend them. Instead, it holds them as fields (Composition / HAS-A).
SmartCamera delegates work to each component without any ambiguity.
This is a clean, industry-standard design pattern.

activities.title: Quick Check: Why No Multiple Class Inheritance? (10 Questions)

questions.question: Can a class in Java directly extend two parent classes (e.g., class C extends A, B)?
options: Yes, if they are in the same package
No, Java does not support multiple class inheritance
Yes, if the methods have different names
questions.explanation: Java strictly disallows multiple class inheritance for classes to prevent ambiguity.

questions.question: What is the classic problem called where two parent classes define the same method and a child extends both?
questions.explanation: The Diamond Problem is the classic ambiguity dilemma in multiple class inheritance.

questions.question: What happens when you attempt to compile 'class C extends A, B' in Java?
options: Compilation error: syntax error / comma not allowed
It throws a RuntimeException when instantiated
questions.explanation: Java compiler flags this as a syntax error during compilation.

questions.question: Why did Java's creators decide to omit multiple class inheritance?
options: To keep the language simple, safe, and avoid method/state ambiguity
Because early computers did not have color monitors
Because Java code is compiled to C
Because JVM bytecode cannot support numbers higher than 1
questions.explanation: Java was designed with simplicity and safety in mind, eliminating the complexities found in C++.

questions.question: Besides method ambiguity, what other conflict arises in multiple class inheritance?
options: Java files can no longer be saved
questions.explanation: If both parent classes define an instance variable with the same name, state duplication and conflict occur.

questions.question: What design technique allows a class to combine features from multiple classes without using inheritance?
questions.explanation: Composition ('HAS-A') allows a class to contain instances of other classes, providing multiple capabilities cleanly.

questions.question: How does Java support multiple inheritance of type (specification)?
options: Through interfaces (a class can implement multiple interfaces)
Java does not support it in any form
questions.explanation: Java supports multiple inheritance of type by allowing a class to implement multiple interfaces.

questions.question: Does the Diamond Problem occur with interfaces that only declare abstract methods?
options: No, because abstract methods have no implementation; the implementing class provides the single implementation
Yes, if the interfaces have different names
questions.explanation: With pure abstract interfaces, there is no implementation conflict; the implementing class writes the method once.

questions.question: In C++, how is the Diamond Problem resolved?
options: By deleting the second parent class
questions.explanation: C++ uses virtual base classes, which introduces significant syntax and conceptual complexity.

questions.question: What famous design principle advises: 'Favor object composition over class inheritance'?
options: The Gang of Four (GoF) design principle
questions.explanation: The Gang of Four (GoF) 'Design Patterns' book famously advises favoring composition over inheritance.

activities.title: Interview Essentials: Diamond Problem & Multiple Inheritance

interviewQA.question: Explain the Diamond Problem and why Java avoids multiple class inheritance.
interviewQA.answer: The Diamond Problem occurs in multiple class inheritance when a class D extends two classes B and C, both of which inherit from a common ancestor A and override the same method. When D invokes that method, the compiler faces ambiguity about whether B's or C's implementation should run. To ensure determinism and avoid complex disambiguation rules like C++ virtual tables, Java disallows extending multiple classes.

interviewQA.question: How does Java solve the need for multiple inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: Java achieves multiple inheritance of type through interfaces. A class can implement multiple interfaces (e.g., 'class Service implements Serializable, Runnable, AutoCloseable'). Because traditional interfaces contain contracts without instance fields (state), state conflict is eliminated. Furthermore, developers can use Composition ('HAS-A') to reuse logic from multiple classes without inheritance coupling.

interviewQA.question: What is the difference between multiple inheritance of state vs multiple inheritance of type?
interviewQA.answer: Multiple inheritance of state occurs when a class inherits instance variables from multiple parent classes, creating memory layout confusion and duplicate state conflicts. Multiple inheritance of type occurs when a class conforms to multiple interface contracts without inheriting instance state. Java forbids multiple inheritance of state, but fully supports multiple inheritance of type.

interviewQA.question: How does Java 8 handle default methods in interfaces regarding the Diamond Problem?
interviewQA.answer: Java 8 introduced default methods in interfaces. If a class implements two interfaces that provide the exact same default method signature, the compiler rejects the class with a duplicate default methods error. The developer is required to explicitly override the conflicting method in the implementing class and choose which one to call (e.g., 'InterfaceA.super.method()').

interviewQA.question: Why is Composition often preferred over Inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: Composition ('favor composition over inheritance') creates loose coupling. A class can assemble capabilities from multiple helper objects at runtime without being bound to their internal implementation details. It avoids fragile base classes, prevents inheritance tree explosion, and eliminates the Diamond Problem entirely.

interviewQA.question: Can an interface extend multiple interfaces in Java?
interviewQA.answer: Yes! While a class can only extend one class, an interface CAN extend multiple interfaces (e.g., 'interface ChildInterface extends ParentA, ParentB'). This is permitted because interfaces define type contracts without instance state.

activities.title: 10-Point Mastery Checklist: Why No Multiple Class Inheritance
checklist: I can explain why Java forbids multiple class inheritance
I can draw and describe the Diamond Problem clearly
I understand instance variable state conflicts in multiple inheritance
I know the difference between multiple inheritance of state vs type

I know what happens if two Java 8 default methods collide
I can explain Java's design decision compared to C++
I understand the principle 'favor composition over inheritance'

practiceProblems.title: Resolving Needs with Composition
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
A developer wants a `SmartThermostat` to have both heating and cooling capabilities. Since Java does not support extending both `Heater` and `Cooler`, use Composition:
1. Create class `Heater` with method `void heat()` printing `"Heating activated."`
2. Create class `Cooler` with method `void cool()` printing `"Cooling activated."`
3. Create class `SmartThermostat` that contains private instances of both `Heater` and `Cooler`. Add methods `void turnOnHeat()` and `void turnOnCool()` delegating to the respective objects.
In `Main.main()`, instantiate `SmartThermostat`, call `turnOnHeat()`, and call `turnOnCool()`.
hints: SmartThermostat HAS-A Heater and HAS-A Cooler (composition).
Delegate method calls from SmartThermostat to the inner instances.

practiceProblems.title: Multi-Function Office Machine From Scratch
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Write a complete program from scratch using composition:
1. Create class `PrinterModule` with method `void printDoc(String text)` printing `"Printing: " + text`.
2. Create class `ScannerModule` with method `void scanDoc(String title)` printing `"Scanning: " + title`.
3. Create class `OfficeMachine` containing private instances of both modules. Add `void doPrint(String doc)` and `void doScan(String doc)`.
4. In `Main.main()`, instantiate `OfficeMachine`, print `"Invoice.pdf"`, and scan `"Receipt.jpg"`.
hints: Both modules are instantiated as fields inside OfficeMachine.

practiceProblems.title: Refactoring Multiple Extends to Composition
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
A student wrote pseudocode trying to inherit from `GPS` and `MusicPlayer` simultaneously. Implement this correctly using composition in a `DashboardConsole` class:
1. Class `GPS`: method `void navigate(String dest)` printing `"Navigating to: " + dest`
2. Class `MusicPlayer`: method `void playSong(String title)` printing `"Playing: " + title`
3. Class `DashboardConsole`: contains `GPS` and `MusicPlayer`. Method `void startTrip(String destination, String song)` that calls `navigate` on the GPS and `playSong` on the music player.
In `Main.main()`, test `startTrip("Grand Canyon", "RoadTripJam.mp3")`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Navigating to: Grand Canyon
Playing: RoadTripJam.mp3
hints: DashboardConsole manages both GPS and MusicPlayer without multiple inheritance.

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Illegal Multiple Extends Clause
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The following program fails compilation because a developer wrote `class Robot extends MechanicalArm, SensorArray`. Fix the code by converting the illegal multiple inheritance into composition, keeping the expected output intact.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Sensor reading: 45 cm distance.
Arm moving to target coordinates.
hints: Declare arm and sensor as private fields inside Robot.

practiceProblems.title: Simulating Multiple Subsystems with Facade
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Design a smart home security hub that integrates three separate hardware components without multiple inheritance:
1. `CameraSystem`: `void enableCameras()` printing `"Cameras streaming live video."`
2. `DoorLockSystem`: `void lockAllDoors()` printing `"All perimeter doors locked."`
3. `AlarmSiren`: `void armSiren()` printing `"Motion alarm siren armed."`
4. `HomeSecurityHub`: contains instances of all three systems. Method `public void activateNightMode()` that calls `enableCameras()`, `lockAllDoors()`, and `armSiren()`, followed by printing `"Night mode security active."`
In `Main.main()`, instantiate `HomeSecurityHub` and call `activateNightMode()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Cameras streaming live video.
All perimeter doors locked.
Motion alarm siren armed.
Night mode security active.
hints: HomeSecurityHub uses composition to unite the three subsystems cleanly.
